summary: A smith who settled at Setauket on Long Island in the 1670s and served as a Brookhaven selectman; John's 10th-great-grandfather.
bio:
John Thompson of Setauket was a smith, working as whitesmith, gunsmith and blacksmith, and John's 10th-great-grandfather. He was at Stamford, Connecticut, in 1667, when he sold his tools to pay his debts, and at Oyster Bay from 1668 to 1673. By 1673 he had settled at Setauket in the town of Brookhaven, where his five-acre home lot lay "south of and adjoining the public green". He was a Brookhaven selectman in 1686. His last appearance in the records is a deed of 1691, and he died intestate some time after that.

His only recorded wife was Mary, named in deeds of 1680 and 1685. His daughter Elizabeth married Job Smith, and his son Samuel married Hannah Brewster, daughter of the Rev. Nathaniel Brewster and widow of John Muncy; Samuel is buried at the southeast corner of the Setauket Presbyterian Church. A long-repeated family tradition made John the son of the Rev. William Thompson of Braintree and the husband of a Hannah Brewster of the Mayflower family, with birth and death dates of 1609 and 1688, but that story has been disproven: the Braintree minister had no son John, and the dates are spurious.

Benjamin F. Thompson, the historian of Long Island, descended from him and called him "the first Long Island ancestor of the compiler". Other Thompson descendants who are John's cousins include Selah Strong, Representative Selah B. Strong, Judge Isaac Thompson, Jonathan Thompson and David Thompson.

researchNotes:
A smith (whitesmith, gunsmith, blacksmith). At Stamford, Conn., in 1667 (sold his tools to pay debts); Oyster Bay 1668–73; Setauket by 1673; Brookhaven selectman 1686; last record a deed of 1691; died intestate. His five-acre home lot lay 'south of and adjoining the public green' at Setauket. Thompson's History of Long Island calls him 'the first Long Island ancestor of the compiler' (B. F. Thompson) and says he married Hannah Brewster on 12 June 1663 and was son of Rev. William Thompson of Braintree (link only 'traditionary', 'not very satisfactorily ascertained'). Champlin (NYGBR 46:4–9, 1915) showed Rev. William of Braintree had no son John and the Mayflower Brewster version false; Jacobus calls the tree-style dates 3 Jun 1609 / 14 Oct 1688 bogus and shows his only recorded wife was Mary (deeds 1680, 1685). Son Samuel married his cousin Hannah Brewster (daughter of Rev. Nathaniel, widow of John Muncy) and is buried at the southeast corner of Setauket Presbyterian Church. Thompson cousins: Selah Strong (2C9R), Rep. Selah B. Strong (4C7R), Judge Isaac Thompson (2C9R), Benjamin F. Thompson (3C8R), Jonathan Thompson (3C8R), David Thompson (4C7R).

Pelletreau calls him 'John Thompson, Esq., of Setauket', father of Elizabeth, wife of Job Smith ([R4-S1]). Weygant (1897) repeats the disproven Rev. William Thompson/Brewster story ([R4-S2]).
